Subject: Commit amortization & ramp schedule — proposed credit tiers

Hi Samantha,

Appreciate the time last week — following up with a concise proposal for the Dedicated commit structure Olive asked about. We modeled two program tracks so you can pick the best fit with procurement:

Option A — 3-year annual prepay (largest term discount)
- Total committed capacity: 80 A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state)
- Ramp schedule: 20 GPUs live within 30 days of SOW, +30 in month 6, +30 in month 12
- Commercials: 18% term discount on list rate with full-year prepayment each year
- Amortization: monthly consumption buckets against annual prepay; unused prepay can be carried for up to 90 days as credits

Option B — Annual prepay with phased invoicing
- Same total capacity target, payment split across year (40% upfront, 30% at month 6, 30% at month 12)
- Discount: 10% effective on list vs. month-to-month
- If you need to accelerate GPUs earlier, we can apply a step-up credit to the next invoice rather than a separate charge

Two asks from our side:
1) Confirm whether Procurement needs a straight-line amortization on your books (we can provide a schedule for GAAP-friendly accounting)
2) Any minimum uptime SLA exceptions we should carve out for the first 90 days during onboarding

Attached: Draft_MSA_v2.pdf (redlines for prepay/cancellation), Ramp_Schedule_Amortization.xlsx (detailed month-by-month amortization).

Happy to jump on 30m Tuesday if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — the two-option framing is helpful. A few clarifying questions from Procurement and Finance:

- For Option A, when you say 'unused prepay can be carried for up to 90 days,' does that mean credits expire on day 91 or are they refundable? Finance prefers credits over refunds but needs a clear expiry window.
- Can you share an example invoice schedule for Option B (line items + tax/rebate handling)?
- Any flexibility on the ramp timing? Our product roadmap might shift some capacity into Q2 of year 2; would that impact the discount tiers?

Also, we'll need the redlined MSA delivered to our legal team — they expect to see cancellation and termination for convenience language.

Samantha
VP, Platform Engineering — Olive Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit amortization & ramp schedule — proposed credit tiers

Samantha — great questions. Short answers below, with details in the attached amortization workbook:

1) Credits vs refunds:
- We can offer non-refundable prepay with credits that expire after 120 days rather than 90; alternatively, we can build a prorated refund clause for terminations after year 1. Refunds require a modest admin fee (1.5% of remaining prepaid value).

2) Option B invoice example:
- Invoice 1 (Day 0): 40% prepay + one-time onboarding fee (prorated first-month consumption)
- Invoice 2 (Month 6): 30% prepay + usage reconciliation line if you consumed more than the prepaid bucket
- Invoice 3 (Month 12): 30% prepay + final reconciliation
- Taxes and credits are handled on each invoice line; we provide a consolidated reconciliation report.

3) Ramp timing flexibility:
- Discount tiers are based on committed capacity (steady-state) rather than strict month-by-month arrival. If you shift ramp into Q2 of year 2 but keep the total commitment, the effective discount holds — we will, however, adjust the amortization schedule and onboarding credits pro rata.

Additional proposal: 90-day pilot credit (up to 6,000 GPU-hours) applied to the first invoice to ease validation risk. I've looped in Marissa from Finance to confirm accounting treatment and Laura for SLA carve-outs.

Attaching updated Ramp_Schedule_Amortization.xlsx with the two alternate amortization views (straight-line vs event-driven).

-Rishi
